previous_statement: From nodes 1.2.3.1 and 1.2.2 one obtains, for every n and Z, ||h_n(Z)||^2 <= b_n||Z^dagger dot Z||+C_prod*e||Z||^2. At n=1, node 1.1 supplies ||Z^dagger dot Z|| <= (1+kappa_1*e)||Z||^2, hence b_1^2 <= (1+kappa_1*e)b_1+C_prod*e (with the zero-corner case giving b_1=0). For n>1, node 1.1 explicitly records that the allowed inputs supply no universal amplified estimate ||Z^dagger dot Z|| <= (1+kappa*e)||Z||^2. Therefore the displayed all-n quadratic inequality does not follow in the permitted dependency scope; an additional uniform amplified-corner norm theorem is required.
new_statement: Take kappa:=C_ca and e_sq:=e_ca as supplied by the allowed validated lem-compcb-corner-algebra dependency through node 1.1. For every e<=min(e_sq,e_prod,e_adj), every n>=1, and every Z in E_n:=M_n tensor S_P, nodes 1.2.3.1 and 1.2.2 together with node 1.1 give ||h_n(Z)||^2<=b_n||Z^dagger dot Z||+C_prod*e||Z||^2<=((1+kappa*e)b_n+C_prod*e)||Z||^2. If E_n={0}, then b_n=0. Otherwise E_n has a nonempty unit sphere, and taking the supremum there (using finite b_n from node 1.2.3.1) yields b_n^2<=(1+kappa*e)b_n+C_prod*e. Thus this scalar quadratic holds uniformly for every n, including the zero-corner case.
